# Ryan Drapeau - Full Portfolio & Research Dossier

> Principal Machine Learning Engineer at Stripe. Builder of privacy-first financial tools, distributed ML systems, and accessible technologies. M.S. & B.S. in Computer Science from the University of Washington.

This document contains the unabridged text, descriptions, technical abstracts, and metadata for all projects, technical writings, patents, and academic publications authored or co-authored by Ryan Drapeau.

---

## 2. Personal Projects & Simulations

### Financial Simulator (FiSim)
- **URL**: https://drapeau.dev/fi_sim/
- **Repository**: Built with Vue 3, Vite, and HTML5 Canvas.
- **Status**: In Active Development.
- **Description**: A privacy-first, client-side personal finance projection planner featuring localized U.S., UK, and Canadian tax engines, Required Minimum Distributions (RMDs), and Monte Carlo historical sequence-of-returns stress testing.
- **Technical Capabilities**: All calculations run 100% locally in the browser with zero server data leakage. Includes tax bracket phaseouts, capital gains treatments, inflation adjustments, and visual fan-chart quantile probability bands.

### Org Planning Simulator
- **URL**: https://drapeau.dev/org_planning/
- **Repository**: Built with React, Vite, and HTML5 Canvas.
- **Status**: Live.
- **Description**: An interactive Monte Carlo simulation tool designed for engineering leaders and executives to model organizational growth, attrition, promotions, and hiring trajectories.
- **Technical Capabilities**: Simulates promotion cycles across engineering levels (L1 through L7+), variable attrition distributions, backfill lead times, and budget constraints across hundreds of randomized organizational iterations.

### Connections
- **URL**: https://drapeau.dev/connections/
- **Repository**: Built with Next.js static export.
- **Status**: Live.
- **Description**: A custom wedding-themed word association puzzle game featuring 4x4 group matching mechanics.
- **Technical Capabilities**: Players find groups of four interconnected items sharing common threads, featuring progressive difficulty tiers, celebratory animations, and shareable solve grids.

### Stitch by Number
- **URL**: https://drapeau.dev/stitch_by_number/
- **Repository**: Built with React, TypeScript, and Vite.
- **Status**: Live.
- **Description**: An image-to-needlepoint design converter that quantizes uploaded imagery into DMC embroidery floss color palettes with printable PDF pattern charts.
- **Technical Capabilities**: Performs CIELAB color-space nearest-neighbor quantization against real-world thread swatches, generates interactive grid previews, and renders high-resolution vector PDF export charts.

### Photo Stacker
- **URL**: https://drapeau.dev/photo_stacker/
- **Repository**: Built with React, TypeScript, and Vite.
- **Status**: Live.
- **Description**: A client-side HDR exposure fusion application running entirely in the browser.
- **Technical Capabilities**: Implements the Mertens-Kautz-Van Reeth multi-scale exposure fusion algorithm using Laplacian pyramids to blend bracketed exposure photographs into natural HDR images without tone-mapping halo artifacts.

### 1Password Extension
- **URL**: https://github.com/rdrapeau/1password_extension
- **Repository**: WebExtension Manifest V3 / Firefox extension.
- **Status**: Live.
- **Description**: A native desktop Firefox browser extension for streamlined credential autofill, keyboard shortcut quick-access, and secure vault interaction.

### Rowing Performance
- **URL**: https://drapeau.dev/rowing_performance/
- **Repository**: Built with React, Tailwind, and Vite.
- **Status**: Live.
- **Description**: A Concept2 rowing ergometer analytics and performance modeling dashboard providing power curves, stroke telemetry analysis, and VO₂ max estimations.
- **Technical Capabilities**: Parses Concept2 workout logs, renders interactive stroke force curves with pointer scrubbing, and computes physiological efficiency metrics.

---

## 3. Technical Writing & Architecture Articles

### Stripe Sigma: SQL for Payments
- **URL**: https://stripe.com/blog/sigma-sql-for-payments
- **Summary**: Details the design and architecture of Stripe Sigma, an interactive distributed SQL environment allowing millions of businesses to query payment telemetry directly. Explains schema virtualization, Presto query federation, and low-latency financial ledger views.

### Building Large-Scale Machine Learning Platforms at Stripe
- **URL**: https://stripe.com/blog/building-machine-learning-infrastructure-at-stripe
- **Summary**: Explores Stripe's unified machine learning training and inference infrastructure. Discusses point-in-time correct feature generation, streaming event buses, model evaluation guards, and multi-region deployment mechanisms operating under strict sub-100ms latency SLAs.

### Scaling Stripe's Identity Graph
- **URL**: https://stripe.com/blog/scaling-stripes-identity-graph
- **Summary**: Examines graph database engineering used to link accounts, hardware tokens, cards, and digital fingerprints across global financial networks, exposing coordinated fraud rings that evade single-account heuristics.

### Machine Learning-Powered Fraud Detection
- **URL**: https://stripe.com/blog/radar-fraud-detection-architecture
- **Summary**: Deep dive into Stripe Radar's adaptive risk scoring architecture, detailing real-time feature engines, merchant-specific behavioral adjustments, and automated 3D Secure dynamic friction routing.

## 4. Patents & Inventions

1. **Systems and methods for identity graph based fraud detection**
   - Patent: US 11,704,673 (Granted July 18, 2023)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US11704673B1/en
   - Abstract: Methods and systems for constructing and traversing multi-entity identity graphs linking transactions across merchants, devices, and financial instruments to uncover distributed fraud rings attempting identity obfuscation.

2. **Systems and methods for secure identifiers for electronic transactions**
   - Patent Application: US 2025/0125969 A1 (Published April 17, 2025)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US20250125969A1/en
   - Abstract: Secure client-side and network-level cryptographic fingerprinting techniques enabling reliable repeat visitor verification and transaction safety without exposing raw consumer hardware identifiers.

3. **Systems and methods for hard deletion of data across systems**
   - Patent Application: US 2024/0126908 A1 (Published April 18, 2024)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US20240126908A1/en
   - Abstract: Distributed consensus mechanisms ensuring verified, irreversible, and auditable hard deletion of personal user records across disparate transactional databases, message queues, and analytical data warehouses.

4. **Systems and methods for privacy preserving fraud detection during electronic transactions**
   - Patent Application: US 2025/0117802 A1 (Published April 10, 2025)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US20250117802A1/en
   - Abstract: Privacy-preserving cryptographic protocols and homomorphic feature evaluation allowing payment risk assessment across shared transaction signals without exposing raw personally identifiable information (PII).

5. **Merchant specific machine learning model for fraud detection**
   - Patent Application: US 2025/0165978 A1 (Published May 22, 2025)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US20250165978A1/en
   - Abstract: Automated transfer learning and meta-learning pipelines that train bespoke merchant-tailored machine learning models adapted to individual transaction volumes, return policies, and seasonal sales patterns.

6. **Systems and methods for enhanced transaction authentication**
   - Patent Application: US 2024/0112192 A1 (Published April 4, 2024)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US20240112192A1/en
   - Abstract: Dynamic friction authentication routing that evaluates real-time risk scores to conditionally invoke two-factor or biometric verification only when transactions display anomalous risk patterns.

7. **Systems and methods for smart remediation for transactions**
   - Patent Application: US 2024/0152924 A1 (Published May 9, 2024)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US20240152924A1/en
   - Abstract: Automated systems that detect post-transaction authorization anomalies, chargebacks, or network disputes and execute automated recovery remediation workflows across banking networks.

8. **Fraud detection using real-time and batch features**
   - Patent Application: US 2024/0161115 A1 (Published May 16, 2024)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US20240161115A1/en
   - Abstract: Hybrid feature architectures that combine millisecond-latency streaming transaction signals with multi-terabyte historical batch aggregations to evaluate ML scoring models in sub-second payment gateways.

9. **Systems and methods for machine learning feature generation**
   - Patent Application: EP 4627492 A1 (Published October 8, 2025)
   - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/EP4627492A1/en
   - Abstract: Automated feature engineering engines that discover high-entropy combinatorial signal patterns across global transaction flows, continually generating new feature candidates to counter adversarial fraud shifts.

10. **Machine learning model training and deployment pipeline**
    - Patent Application: US 2024/0070484 A1 (Published February 29, 2024)
    - Link: https://patents.google.com/patent/US20240070484A1/en
    - Abstract: Continuous training, validation, canary testing, and deployment pipelines enabling zero-downtime hot-swapping of mission-critical AI risk scoring models at massive global transaction scale.

## 5. Academic Research & Publications

1. **Microtalk: Argumentation in Crowdsourcing**
   - Venue: AAAI Conference on Human Computation and Crowdsourcing (HCOMP '16)
   - Authors: Ryan Drapeau, Lydia B. Chilton, Jonathan Bragg, Daniel S. Weld
   - Link: https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=yghhd38AAAAJ&citation_for_view=yghhd38AAAAJ:9yKSN-GCB0IC
   - Abstract: Introduces a peer argumentation protocol (Assess -> Justify -> Reconsider) where crowd workers exchange structured rationales. Demonstrates that deliberation boosts individual and aggregate classification accuracy by +20% on challenging natural language understanding and image categorization tasks lacking ground truth.

2. **Tactile Graphics with a Voice**
   - Venue: ACM Transactions on Accessible Computing (TACCESS '16)
   - Authors: Catherine M. Baker, Lauren R. Milne, Ryan Drapeau, Jeffrey Scofield, Cynthia L. Bennett, Richard E. Ladner
   - Link: https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=yghhd38AAAAJ&citation_for_view=yghhd38AAAAJ:u-x6o8ySG0sC
   - Abstract: Presents a multimodal accessibility system combining physical relief graphics with smartphone camera QR scanning and finger-pointing detection to provide localized spoken-audio descriptions for complex STEM tactile diagrams for blind and low-vision learners.

3. **The Wisdom of Multiple Guesses**
   - Venue: ACM Conference on Economics and Computation (EC '15)
   - Authors: Johan Ugander, Ryan Drapeau, Carlos Guestrin
   - Link: https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=yghhd38AAAAJ&citation_for_view=yghhd38AAAAJ:d1gkVwhDpl0C
   - Abstract: Investigates crowdsourced prediction mechanisms that elicit multiple ranked guesses per individual rather than single estimates. Shows that eliciting within-person distributions captures personal uncertainty, producing certainty-weighted aggregations that consistently outperform standard crowd averages.

4. **KIMBEE: Speech Therapy for Children**
   - Venue: University of Washington Technical Report (UW CSE '15)
   - Authors: Ryan Drapeau, Nicolas Huynh, Aaron Nech
   - Link: https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=yghhd38AAAAJ&citation_for_view=yghhd38AAAAJ:qjMakFHDy7sC
   - Abstract: A mobile acoustic speech therapy system providing children with real-time phonological feedback through articulation game mechanics while streaming phoneme accuracy telemetry to speech-language pathologists.

5. **Contributing During the Commute**
   - Venue: University of Washington Technical Report (UW CSE '15)
   - Authors: Caitlin Bonnar, Meg Campbell, Ryan Drapeau, Cynthia L. Bennett, Alan Borning
   - Link: https://scholar.google.com/citations?view_op=view_citation&hl=en&user=yghhd38AAAAJ&citation_for_view=yghhd38AAAAJ:UeHWp8X0CEIC
   - Abstract: An empirical study within the OneBusAway mobile transit platform investigating prosocial volunteer dynamics when transit riders crowdsource bus stop physical accessibility attributes (curb ramps, shelters, seating).
